scenes.heading: Adobe IMS Fundamentals (Part 1 of 2)
scenes.narration: Authentication. Adobe IMS Fundamentals (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 5 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is Adobe IMS?
scenes.heading: Adobe's Identity Management System, used to log in administrators and regular users to AEM Author
scenes.body: Adobe IMS (Identity Management System) is the identity platform AEMaaCS uses to authenticate both administrators and regular users into the Author service. Because AEMaaCS is cloud-native, it relies on IMS rather than local AEM-only credentials.

scenes.question: What are Adobe IMS users?
scenes.heading: Individuals who require access to the AEM Author service, managed centrally in Adobe Admin Console
scenes.body: Adobe IMS users are individuals who need access to the AEM Author service. They are created, updated, and deleted centrally within Adobe's Admin Console, which serves as the hub for user administration across Experience Cloud products.

scenes.question: What are Adobe IMS user groups?
scenes.heading: A way to organize users accessing the AEM Author service into logical groups
scenes.body: Adobe IMS user groups organize users into logical groupings in Admin Console. On their own, they don't grant permissions or access — they exist purely to make user management easier, and are typically mapped to AEM groups and permissions.

scenes.question: Do Adobe IMS user groups directly grant AEM permissions?
scenes.heading: No — IMS user groups do not grant permissions by themselves; they are organizational only
scenes.body: IMS user groups by themselves grant no permissions or access to AEM. They are an organizational construct. Actual access is granted by assigning users (not groups) to IMS Product Profiles.

scenes.question: What is an Adobe IMS product profile?
scenes.heading: The mechanism that grants Adobe IMS users access to log in to the AEM Author service
scenes.body: IMS product profiles are the mechanism that actually grants login access to AEM Author. They define a base level of access, and by assigning the right profile administrators control what a user can do once authenticated.
